LESSON: MY CLASSMATES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: My Neighbourhood
Topic 4.1: My Classmates
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers My Classmates, part of My Neighbourhood in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have neighbours?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on My Classmates together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Citizenship: learner develops relationships when playing games harmoniously with classmates.

Values:
Love: learner portrays a caring attitude when sharing play materials with classmates.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion: learner enhances kindness and friendliness when playing games with classmates.

Link to other learning area:

Friends as our neighbours when learning about loving neighbours in Religious Activities

  -  Learners are guided to play games

with classmates using any alternative

functional part of the body. The time

of game, and size of play area should

be reduced for learners with mobility

and manipulation difficulties as well

as those with anemia and cardiac

complications. The play materials

such as balls should also be larger and

lighter to enhance manipulation.

Learners with difficulties in

movement could use mobility devices.

manipulation and movement

difficulties could record the scores or

keep the play time as time keepers.

as classmates. Learners with speech

difficulties could use residual speech

or write their prayer and the rest read

out the prayer.
